[[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] '''limoncello''' recipe.

==Ingredients==
*15 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] superfine [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Fifth|fifths]] (1.5 [[Cookbook:Liter|litres]] total) 100 proof [[Cookbook:Vodka|vodka]]
*5 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

==Procedure==
# Wash the lemons with a vegetable brush and hot water to remove any residue of pesticides or wax. Carefully [[Cookbook:Zest|zest]] the lemons with a [[Cookbook:Zester|zester]] or vegetable [[Cookbook:Peeler|peeler]] so there is no white pith on the peel.
# In a 1-gallon glass jar, combine half the vodka and the lemon zest. Cover the jar and let sit at room temperature for at least 10 days, and up to 40 days in a cool dark place.
# In a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], combine the sugar and water and cook until thickened (about 5–7 minutes). Let the [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]] cool before adding it to the limoncello mixture. Add the additional fifth of vodka. Allow to rest for another 10–40 days.
# After the rest period, strain and bottle, discarding the lemon zest. Keep in the freezer until ready to serve.

==Notes, tips and variations==
* Wondering what to do with the lemons after you've zested them? Try making [[Cookbook:Lemonade|lemonade]], [[Cookbook:Ginger beer|ginger beer]], or [[Cookbook:Sima|sima]].

In a 1-gallon glass jar, combine half the vodka and the lemon zest. Cover the jar and let sit at room temperature for at least 10 days, and up to 40 days in a cool dark place.

In a large saucepan, combine the sugar and water and cook until thickened (about 5–7 minutes). Let the syrup cool before adding it to the limoncello mixture. Add the additional fifth of vodka. Allow to rest for another 10–40 days.
